name: Double-acting steam specification
summary: James Watt's 1782 patent description of a steam engine that pushes and pulls on both piston strokes, giving smoother, stronger power suited to driving machinery.
description: Watt describes alternating steam admission and condensation above and below the piston, transmitting both push and pull through rack-and-sector or other connections.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

impact.note: One patent text describing a clear improvement to engine working, known to the engine trade, with a few direct successors.

why: Mill owners wanted smoother, continuous power to drive machinery, and Boulton and Watt sought patent protection for engine arrangements that could serve that market.

date.basis: Patent granted 12 March; specification enrolled 4 July 1782.

events.statement: Watt describes alternating steam admission and condensation above and below the piston, transmitting both push and pull through rack-and-sector or other connections.
events.caveats: A patent describes claimed arrangements; it does not alone establish operation or the stated doubling of actual output.

evidence.locator: Section 26: Second Improvement, figures 12–13, and Fourth New Improvement
evidence.supports: Alternating action, condenser passages, piston connection and rack-and-sector arrangement.

date.basis: The repository catalogue identifies the first double-acting Soho engine at work in 1783, with March and June reported differently.

events.statement: A double-acting rack-and-sector engine worked a corn mill at Soho in 1783.
events.scope: Double-acting steam admission with a rack-and-sector connection, as described in Watt’s 1782 specification.
events.caveats: The source dates actual operation to 1783 but disagrees on the month; this does not establish a public offer or use of every alternative in the specification.

evidence.locator: MS 3147/5/1340, technical description and final paragraph
evidence.supports: Describes the 18-inch double-acting rack-and-sector engine with internal sun-and-planet gear driving a corn mill; records disagree on March/June 1783.

evidence.locator: 1782 specification: description of the double-acting engine
evidence.supports: Provides the contemporary specification against which the identified configuration is compared.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. Patent granted 12 March; specification enrolled 4 July 1782. A patent describes claimed arrangements; it does not alone establish operation or the stated doubling of actual output. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.community: Soho Manufactory corn-mill workers and engine builders
community_entry.rationale: A documented application of the specified mechanism to milling follows the earlier patent description.
community_entry.caveats: The source dates actual operation to 1783 but disagrees on the month; this does not establish a public offer or use of every alternative in the specification.

links.statement: Watt added alternate driving strokes to his engine by routing spent steam from opposite cylinder ends to condensation passages.
links.alternatives: Other engine arrangements could be double acting; the edge is bounded to this specified design.
links.caveats: Does not treat a patent claim as a working demonstration.
links.timing: Later mechanism extends the 1769 configuration; both patent stages precede the Soho operating evidence.

evidence.locator: Section 26: Second Improvement, paragraphs on valves E/N and condenser in figure 13
evidence.supports: Application to his prior engine and alternate condensation/admission arrangement.
